catalysts: short‑interest squeeze if any positive news appears

bear.case: The stock trades far below all major moving averages, has no catalyst, and carries extreme short interest, indicating continued downside.

premortem.failure_story: A sudden positive catalyst (e.g., earnings beat or FDA approval) triggers a rapid short‑cover rally, pushing NBIL above the stop level and causing a loss.

decision.reason: Risk‑off regime, heavy short interest, price far below SMA20/50/200 and no catalyst make further decline more probable than a rebound.
decision.odds_reasoning: Base win rate for short breakdowns ~38%; added short‑interest bias and risk‑off context raise confidence to ~45%.
decision.thesis: NBIL is heavily shorted (≈60% of float) and trading well below its 20‑day (23.13) and 50‑day (24.41) SMAs. In a defensive market the lack of any fundamental catalyst makes a further slide toward its 20‑day low more likely than a bounce.
decision.invalidation: If price closes above $15.50 (≈2 ATR) or a positive earnings/news surprise occurs, exit the short.
decision.plain_english: The stock is far under its average prices and most traders are betting it will go down. Because the market is cautious and there’s no good news, we expect it to keep falling. We’ll sell the stock at $13, set a stop at $15.50 to limit loss, and aim to buy it back near $9.50 for a profit.
